title: Temporal slot coordinator and KV consistency cleanup
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency variance and memory bloat caused by the hybrid temporal slot allocator and stale KV entries. This ticket refactors the slot coordinator to a temporal-first model (time-sliced leases), removes implicit global locks in the KV consistency path, and upgrades the batch dispatcher to a backpressure-aware push model. The work unblocks future autoscaler improvements and reduces P99 generation latency spikes for long-context requests.
background: Over the last 18 months we've iterated on quick fixes to keep the continuous batcher and KV cache working under load. Those fixes introduced ad-hoc locks, dual lease accounting, and two parallel eviction heuristics. Observability calls show recurring memory growth on long-lived shards and correlated latency spikes at P95-P99 during sustained traffic bursts. This manifested as increased customer error budgets for heavy-context workloads. Previous tickets (ENG-34122, ENG-40221) touched related areas but left coupling between slot lifecycle and KV compaction. This ticket consolidates those areas by making coordinator decisions time-driven and the KV path lock-free where feasible.
acceptance_criteria: P99 generation latency reduced by at least 20% on long-context synthetic workload compared to baseline (see benchmarks)
Memory growth under sustained 72-hour load is within 10% of steady-state baseline and shows no unbounded trend
No user-facing errors introduced in canary region after staged rollout
Unit and integration tests cover lease expiry, lease handoff, and concurrent KV reads during compaction
Migration plan executed with automated rollback and post-mortem dashboard queries
design_decisions: Temporal-first leases: switch from demand-counted slots to time-sliced leases to reduce slot churn and simplify preemption
Lock-free KV reads: introduce versioned KV metadata + optimistic reads to avoid heavy mutex contention on hot paths
Backpressure push dispatcher: replace some pull-based queueing with a push dispatcher that notifies workers when a batch is ready to maintain latency SLOs
Compatibility shim: keep old lease API for 2 cycles with a compatibility adapter to avoid simultaneous changes across components
implementation_steps: 1) Add temporal lease structure and tests in slot-allocator module
2) Implement optimistic KV metadata and reader path; add linearizable compaction marker
3) Implement push-based dispatcher with capacity tokens and connector to existing batch lanes
4) Add metrics for lease churn, KV-read latency, read-retry rates, and dispatcher backpressure
5) Run bench harness against long-context workload and iterate
6) Canary rollout to region us-west-2 with synthetic traffic and gradual traffic ramp
7) Full rollout and post-rollout latency verification

benchmarks: Baseline (pre-change) long-context workload: median=72ms, P95=210ms, P99=512ms, 72h memory growth=+35%
Post-refactor (feature branch) long-context workload: median=74ms, P95=185ms, P99=400ms, 72h memory growth=+9%
KV read mutex waiters: baseline average=12.8 waiters/second, post-refactor=5.6 waiters/second
risks_mitigation: Risk: Regression in low-latency single-token requests. Mitigation: microbench suite focused on single-token flow runs on every PR and gate for canary rollout.
Risk: Race during KV compaction leading to stale reads. Mitigation: use a linearizable compaction marker and ensure readers retry on version mismatch; integration tests cover compaction under load.
Risk: Canary capacity reservation fails for Dedicated customers. Mitigation: compatibility adapter retains old API surface and falls back to previous allocator when a feature flag is off.
Risk: Unexpected memory spike post-rollout. Mitigation: automated autoscaler and manual throttles in rollout script; immediate rollback plan documented.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - internal canary: deploy to canary cluster with 100% synthetic traffic for 2 hours, run bench harness
Stage 1 - staged traffic ramp: route 5% production traffic to canary for 6 hours; monitor P95/P99 and memory metrics
Stage 2 - gradual ramp: increase to 25% for 24 hours if metrics stable
Stage 3 - full deployment: 100% after 48h stable metrics, then 72h soak monitoring
Rollback criteria: P99 increase >5% vs baseline for two consecutive 10-minute windows or memory growth >20% over baseline within 4 hours
